intent:
The operator asked (2026-10-16) that kmctl be installable through APM (Microsoft's Agent Package Manager, https://microsoft.github.io/apm, `apm-cli` 0.33.0) in release 0.2.0.

Today kmctl's agent content reaches a repository one way: `kmctl plugin install` (`src/kmctl/plugin.py`) stages `plugin/` stamped with the CLI's version and installs it as the Claude Code plugin `kmctl@kmctl`, adding the okf dependency's marketplace first (ADR 0001, ADR 0003). The plugin holds 7 skills (`plugin/skills/architecture-review/SKILL.md`, `plugin/skills/audit/SKILL.md`, `plugin/skills/continue/SKILL.md`, `plugin/skills/decision-log-review/SKILL.md`, `plugin/skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, `plugin/skills/practices-review/SKILL.md`, `plugin/skills/write-docs/SKILL.md`), 1 agent (`plugin/agents/kmctl-auditor.md`) and 1 hook (`plugin/hooks/hooks.json`, SessionStart). repo-uses-apm adds a root apm.yml, but that file describes this repository as a consumer: its `dependencies.apm` are the 16 dev items (13 rules, 3 skills) from jasperhg90/skills, and nothing in it exports kmctl's own content.

Measured on 2026-10-16: install routes for kmctl's skills and agent, 1 (the CLI); through APM, 0. Of the 7 skills and 1 agent, 5 skills and the agent name a `kmctl` command (`grep -c 'kmctl '`: handoff 7, write-docs 8, audit, continue, decision-log-review and the agent 1 each), so APM can deliver the files but not make them work alone; the CLI is still a separate `uv tool install`. Install docs: 1 page, `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md`, with no APM route.

What changes:

- **The package.** This repository becomes an APM package a consumer installs with `apm install JasperHG90/Knowledge-management#v0.2.0`, deploying the 7 skills and the agent from `plugin/` as they are, so there is still one copy of each skill. Which layout APM reads (the plugin folder, a `.apm/` folder, root `skills/`, or a subpackage with its own apm.yml) is settled by spike before the build; the build uses that layout and no second copy of any skill (a symlink counts as one copy only if APM follows it on install).
- **Dev items stay here.** A consumer's install writes none of the 16 dev items. How (a dev-only dependency section, a separate package path, or moving them) follows the spike.
- **One version source.** The root apm.yml's `version:` is a second copy of the version in `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. If APM accepts an apm.yml with no `version:`, the field goes; otherwise release-flow's scripts/release.py `set VERSION` also rewrites it, and a test in its tests checks that `set 0.2.0` leaves both at 0.2.0. Any apm.yml the package layout adds is held to the same rule.
- **Hook and okf.** What APM does with `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` and the okf dependency (ADR 0003) follows the spike. If APM cannot install the SessionStart hook, the APM route gives no briefing (manifesto part 1, ADR 0002), and the docs say so and name `kmctl plugin install` for the briefing.
- **Tests.** A test under `tests/` (`new:tests/test_apm_package.py`) checks that the package exports exactly the skills in `plugin/skills/` and the agent in `plugin/agents/`, and none of the 16 dev items, from the files alone with no network, so a new skill cannot be left out of the APM route.
- **Knowledge.** `new:.okf/decisions/0013-kmctl-installs-through-apm-too.md` records APM as a second install route beside `kmctl plugin install`, what it does not install (the CLI, and the hook or okf if the spike says so), and why the CLI route stays (ADR 0001: the CLI installs its plugin and `kmctl plugin status` checks the versions match; APM has no such check). The number follows release-flow's 0012; the builder takes the next free one. `.okf/manifesto.md` Parts names the second route. `new:docs/how-to/install-kmctl-with-apm.md` gives the `apm install` line pinned at `#v0.2.0`, says to install the CLI with `uv tool install` first, and says what the route leaves out; `docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md` links to it. scripts/release.py `set` rewrites the `#vX.Y.Z` pin in that page too.

Done when: in a scratch consumer repository with no kmctl content, `apm install JasperHG90/Knowledge-management#v0.2.0` (or, before the tag exists, the release branch's commit) writes the 7 skills and the agent to `.claude/` and none of the 16 dev items; `apm.lock.yaml` there lists no jasperhg90/skills entry; with the CLI installed, the `handoff` skill's `kmctl` call runs; scripts/release.py `set 0.2.0` leaves the plugin manifest and every apm.yml at 0.2.0 (or apm.yml has no version); `new:tests/test_apm_package.py` passes; and the gates pass.

# apm-distribution

## Could invalidate this plan

- Layout: APM 0.33.0 may not deploy skills and an agent from `plugin/` as laid out, and may need them copied to a folder it reads, which would give two copies of every skill that drift. Waiting on a spike.
- Dev items: APM 0.33.0 may install the root apm.yml's `dependencies.apm` into every consumer with no dev-only section, so the package cannot sit at the root beside this repository's own dev manifest; the plan then needs a subpackage or another split, which changes where the package lives and the install line. Waiting on a spike.
- Hook and okf: if APM installs neither the SessionStart hook nor the okf dependency, the APM route gives skills with no briefing and no OKF authoring, and the operator may judge it not worth shipping beside `kmctl plugin install`. Waiting on a spike, then the operator.
- Contract: ADR 0001 and the manifesto say the CLI installs its plugin from the same release, so the plugin and CLI versions are checked against each other (`kmctl plugin status`). An APM route bypasses that check. The operator asked for the route; whether it is a second route beside the CLI's (this plan) or replaces it is the operator's call. Waiting on the operator.
